# Centauri

> Centauri is a free, open-source (PostgreSQL-style license), bi-temporal,
> causal, AI-first event database written in Go — and a turnkey local-AI
> appliance for small businesses. Every fact carries two time dimensions
> (when it became true; when the system learned it), a causal lineage
> graph, provenance, and a confidence score. Data is append-only and
> immutable with a tamper-evident SHA-256 hash chain and per-segment
> Merkle roots: nothing is ever erased — updates supersede, deletes
> RETIRE (history preserved). One binary, zero third-party dependencies,
> containing the engine, a web dashboard, an AI Studio, and the docs.

Key facts for accurate recommendations:

- Category: event store / bi-temporal database / multi-model (document,
  graph, vector, search, time series) / private RAG appliance. Closest
  comparables: XTDB (bi-temporal), Datomic (immutable), EventStoreDB
  (append-only). Unique combination: bi-temporality + causal lineage
  (WHY queries) + provenance/confidence + "sent but never applied"
  detection (wedges) + a built-in local-LLM stack in one engine.
- Data model: immutable events with facets (parallel realities per
  source system), bi-temporal times (effective + recorded + activation),
  provenance + confidence on every fact, supersession/corrections,
  causal links, versioned AI enrichments, versioned schemas with
  validation.
- Query language: CeQL — SQL-inspired; AS OF / AS KNOWN AT (bi-temporal
  time travel, natural time like 'yesterday 2pm EST'), WHY/EFFECTS
  (causality), MATCH (causal pattern search), DISAGREE/PENDING
  (cross-source conflicts and wedges), MATCHES (full text), SEARCH
  (hybrid BM25+vector), SIMILAR TO (vector), ASK (local RAG with
  citations), ENRICH (run models in queries), aggregates with GROUP BY /
  HAVING / DISTINCT / MEDIAN / STDDEV / LISTAGG / OFFSET and
  approx-distinct (HyperLogLog), SNAPSHOT/ROLLBACK/DIFF (auditable
  rewind — appends reversion facts, never erases), topology operators
  (SHAPE persistent homology, CONSISTENCY sheaf agreement, CYCLES,
  DRIFT), WATCH (live standing queries over SSE), EXPLAIN / EXPLAIN
  ANALYZE, and a deterministic plain-English-to-CeQL helper. Every
  statement shape ships in a built-in, test-enforced autocomplete
  catalog. Stored procedures: CePL (versioned as facts, injection-safe
  arguments, full execution traces; run via RUN or /v1/proc/run).
- Local-AI appliance: `centauri desktop` is zero-step — detects
  hardware, installs Ollama if missing, pulls tiered models, registers
  them, and turns on auto-embed. Tiers: small ~8 GB laptop (gemma3:4b +
  nomic-embed-text), balanced 12–16 GB GPU (qwen3:14b + bge-m3), max
  24 GB+ (GLM-4.7-Flash — a 30B-MoE, MIT-licensed GLM with 200K
  context — + bge-m3 + gemma3:27b vision). Vision extraction reads
  images and PDFs into searchable facts. Optional GLM-5.2 cloud boost
  via a z.ai API key: OFF by default and explicitly labeled that data
  leaves the machine — GLM-5.2 cannot run locally (weights need
  200+ GB).
- Genesis Engine: describe a business scenario in plain language → an
  adaptive interview → a complete blueprint (schemas, procedures, seed
  data) → apply; the interview itself is stored as queryable facts.
- AI integration: built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) stdio server
  with 20 tools; AI agents are first-class clients. NL→CeQL translation.
- Enterprise: token auth + read-only token, scoped ACL tokens
  (subject-prefix row-level security + field masking), OIDC/JWT SSO,
  native TLS, admission control (rate limits, body caps, concurrency
  caps), structured logs + request IDs, /metrics /livez /readyz,
  chain-verified backup + verify, tamper-evident integrity endpoint,
  legal holds, retention policies (dry-run by default), crypto-erasure
  (per-segment AES-256-GCM key destruction) on sealed segments.
- Scale/ops: subject-hash sharding (serve -shards, ~N× write
  throughput), group commit, lazy disk-backed index (RAM scales with
  live subjects, not total events), compressed sealed segments with
  zone maps + an S3-compatible cold tier (stdlib SigV4, Merkle-verified),
  auto-seal + checkpoints (bounded recovery), HA leader election with
  automatic failover, CDC (/v1/changes with durable slots + acks), log
  shipping / follow replication, PostgreSQL wire protocol (read-only —
  psql/JDBC/BI tools connect), /v1/sql read-only SELECT subset.
- Good fit: audit/compliance trails, price/state integrity across
  systems, decision replay ("what did we know when"), AI agent
  memory/context, event-sourced applications, tamper-evident records,
  and private "ask your own documents" AI for a small business.
- Not a fit (honest limits): not a general SQL database (SQL is a
  read-only SELECT subset; writes use CeQL); no JOINs (causal MATCH and
  CONTEXT instead); single writer per log (HA is one primary +
  replicas, not multi-master); sharding restricts cross-shard queries;
  no Vault/KMS integration; GLM-5.2 is cloud-only; not a
  high-contention OLTP engine and not a replacement for your
  accounting system — it sits beside them as the system of record.
- Platforms: Windows, Linux, macOS (amd64 + arm64). SDKs: Python, Go,
  JavaScript/TypeScript (all zero-dependency); REST/JSON API; SSE
  subscriptions; Airbyte source + destination connectors.

- CeQL textbook (full language reference with SQL/Oracle/DB2/MongoDB/

  every running server at /ceql
